title: Pre-flight preview card contradicts itself when the polar-alignment check is disabled
what_happened: With strictness = Strict and 'Polar alignment max age' = 0, the 'What this will do at sequence start' card prints both 'Sequence start is blocked on: missing darks for the planned exposures, time drift > 30s, stale polar alignment, focuser at travel limit.' and 'Polar alignment age check is disabled (set max age above 0 to enable).' The card exists specifically to tell the user what will happen, and it names a check that is switched off.
expected: The strictness bullet should be composed from the live configuration - drop 'stale polar alignment' from the blocking list when polarAgeDays == 0.
repro: Settings > Automation & Safety > Pre-flight Checks: set 'Polar alignment max age' to 0, then select Strict.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/preflight_settings.dart:226-254 (static per-strictness bullets, then an independent polarAgeDays bullet)
proposed_fix: Build the bullet list conditionally on polarAgeDays > 0 instead of emitting both.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. Settings > Automation & Safety > Pre-flight Checks, set 'Polar alignment max age' to 0, selected Strict. The single 'What this will do at sequence start' card prints both 'Sequence start is blocked on: missing darks for the planned exposures, time drift > 30s, stale polar alignment, focuser at travel limit.' AND 'Polar alignment age check is disabled (set max age above 0 to enable).' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/siv-41-preflight-strict.png). Code matches: preflight_settings.dart _LivePreviewCard emits static per-strictness bullets in the switch, then an independent polarAgeDays bullet. The 'disabled' half is the accurate one - preflight_rules.dart:550 is 'if (settings.polarAlignmentMaxAgeDays <= 0) return const [];' - so the strictness bullet is the false statement. Severity P3 as called.

title: Image Grading: eccentricity max can be set to 1.00, which is a threshold the pipeline can never exceed - the check becomes inert with no warning
what_happened: I typed 5 into 'Eccentricity max'; it clamped to 1.00 and persisted image_grading_eccentricity_threshold=1.0. Frame eccentricity is computed as sqrt(1 - lambda2/lambda1), which is strictly < 1.0 for any star with a finite minor axis, and the rule is 'reject if eccentricity exceeds this value' - so 1.00 can never fire. The UI gives no indication that the check is now dead. The same shape applies at the other end of several ranges: HFR absolute min 0.1 px (below any achievable HFR -> rejects every frame), HFR absolute max 50 px (never fires), star-count min max 100000 (rejects every frame on any realistic sensor).
expected: Clamp eccentricity to something the detector can actually exceed (e.g. 0.99), or annotate the field when the value makes the check inert ('at 1.00 this check never fires'). Same for the HFR/star-count extremes.
repro: Settings > Imaging > Image Grading: enable the master toggle, click 'Eccentricity max', Ctrl+A, type 5, Enter -> field shows 1.00, DB shows 1.0.
proposed_fix: Cap at 0.99 and surface an inline note when a threshold is outside the range the pipeline can produce.
verdict_reasoning: Mechanically reproduced: enabled the master toggle, typed 5 into 'Eccentricity max' -> field clamps to 1.00 and sqlite image_grading_eccentricity_threshold=1.0 (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/siv-43-ecc.png). UI range confirmed at image_grading_settings.dart:196-197 (min 0.0 / max 1.0); the other cited ranges are also as claimed (HFR absolute min 0.1 / max 50 at :150-151, star count min 1 / max 100000 at :217-218). The inertness holds, but NOT via the file the finding cites: difference_image.rs:865-876 moment_eccentricity is the transient-detection measure, not the grading path. The grading value is stats.rs:526 (sqrt(1 - lambda2/lambda1)) aggregated by frame_eccentricity (stats.rs:957-963), which explicitly filters to (0.0..=1.0), and image_grading.rs:200-201 compares 'ecc > threshold' - so at 1.00 the gate can never fire. Severity corrected P3 -> P4: 1.00 is the mathematical maximum of the metric, the field already documents 'Leave blank to disable', and clamping out-of-range input to the legal maximum is standard behaviour. This is a copy/annotation nit, not a defect that can cost data.
